name: The Prodigal Son
overview: The parable of the Prodigal Son, introduced in Luke 15:11-12, reveals a father's generous response to his wayward son who demands his inheritance early and departs. This story, set within a context where sinners and tax collectors seek Jesus' teaching (Luke 15:1), emphasizes God's joyful reception of repentant sinners, as heaven rejoices over one sinner who repents more than over many righteous individuals who do not need repentance (Luke 15:7). The narrative highlights themes of grace, forgiveness, and restoration that reflect the heart of the gospel message.
